title: Toward a Theory of Evaluability
gist: Kunal Talwar (Apple, NeurIPS paper, Nov 2026) formalizes 'evaluability' of black-box ML models when test samples may have leaked into training — a growing issue for large foundation models. Output-only evaluation is feasible iff the distribution is close to small support, while a small amount of query access (linked to self-correctors from program testing) substantially increases evaluator power.

insights.claim: The classical machine learning evaluation assumption that the test set is held out from training is increasingly hard to justify for large foundation models.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Public benchmark scores for frontier LLMs may be inflated by contamination; discount leaderboard claims in vendor comparisons.
insights.quote: an assumption that is increasingly harder to justify for large foundation models
insights.locator: The classical approach to these problems

insights.claim: Foundation models are increasingly evaluated on multiple axes beyond task accuracy, including safety, calibration and fairness, all of which depend on trustworthy test data.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Contamination undermines not just capability claims but safety/fairness certifications relevant to regulation.
insights.locator: Machine learning models, particularly large foundation models

insights.claim: When an evaluator only sees a black-box model's outputs on a possibly-contaminated test set, accurate evaluation is feasible if and only if the data distribution is close to being small support.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: For rich, natural distributions, passive benchmarks cannot certify contaminated models — expect demand for new evaluation methods and private/held-out eval services.
insights.quote: black-box evaluation in this setup is feasible if and only if the distribution is close to being small support
insights.locator: Our results show that black-box evaluation

insights.claim: Talwar gives a full characterization and tight upper and lower bounds on the sample complexity of evaluating black-box models whose test samples may have been used in training.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Provides a theoretical yardstick for how much fresh evaluation data is needed when contamination cannot be ruled out.
insights.locator: We fully characterize the class of distributions

insights.claim: Allowing an evaluator to query a model on additional inputs, using ideas from self-correctors in program testing, means a small amount of query access can substantially increase evaluation power for natural distributions and concept classes.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Interactive/API-based auditing beats static benchmarks — favors third-party eval firms with query access and regulators requiring model access.
insights.quote: a small amount of query access can increase the power of the evaluator

insights.claim: Apple's evaluability theory work sits alongside its broader push on Apple Intelligence foundation models and unified speech-model evaluation taxonomies, reflecting evaluation as a research priority.
insights.speaker: Apple ML Research
insights.so_what: Apple is investing in rigorous evaluation methodology for its own foundation models.
